title: NCPatcher module graph
description: The resolved module graph: which modules and components a build enabled, what each contributes, and where every source, include and define came from. Written by modules.dump, or by `ncpatcher modules dump`. This is the whole of what a code generator needs to know about a project's structure, and everything game-specific in it rides in `extra`, which NCPatcher preserves and never interprets.

dir.description: The modules directory, absolute and slash-separated. Every other path in this file is absolute too: a dump is written for one machine's build and is not a portable artifact.

modules.description: Every module the project names, in `modules.enabled` order, which is also the order that settles two modules claiming one NitroFS destination. Disabled modules appear too, carrying only the four fields that need no module.yaml.

targets.description: What the modules add up to, per processor: the include path, the defines and the sources, already merged and assigned to regions. A module's includes are target-wide rather than module-private, which is why one module can include another's headers.

key.description: The directory name, and the name the project writes in `modules.enabled`.

id.description: The module's own `id`, which is what generated code and level data name it by. Distinct from `key`: a directory can be renamed without invalidating anything that refers to the module.

enabled.description: Whether the project enabled it. A disabled module ends here, since its module.yaml was never read, so there is nothing further to report, and saying it exists answers why it contributed nothing.

nitrofs.description: The tree this module sweeps into the ROM, if it declares one. Which files that produced is not here, but in the file manifest, where each entry names the module it came from.

dir.description: Absolute, already joined to the module directory.

layered.description: Whether the first path segment under `dir` is a variant name rather than part of the ROM path.

base-variant.description: The layer applied underneath the built variant.

into.description: A ROM path prefix for everything the tree produces.

extra.description: Root keys of module.yaml that NCPatcher does not define, re-emitted as JSON with YAML's scalar types resolved. This is the extension point: a key here means something to whichever tool reads the dump, and nothing at all to NCPatcher. nsmb-coop-module's glue module declares `level-data` this way.

enabled.description: Whether this component contributed. A disabled one still appears, with its sources and files listed: those files are subtracted from the module's tree rather than inserted, so the entry says what switching the feature off removed.

disabled-because.description: Why, when it is not simply that the project switched it off, such as an unmet `requires`.

overlay.description: The overlay this component's code goes into, or null for the main binary.

locked.description: Whether the module fixed the target, refusing a project-level override. Code written against one overlay's memory map does not move.

origin.description: Who decided: `project`, `module`, or `module (the override was refused)`.

target.description: Null when the component names no target, which a component that only defines a symbol may do.

sources.description: Absolute paths, globs already expanded and sorted.

files.description: Glob patterns naming the ROM destinations this component owns, matched against the NitroFS path with any variant segment stripped. Ownership while enabled; subtraction from the module's tree while disabled.

extra.description: Component keys NCPatcher does not define, re-emitted as JSON. Where nsmb-coop-module's `objects` lives.

location.description: Where the component is declared, so a generator can point at the source of a problem rather than restating it.

includes.description: Every enabled module's include contributions, in module order. Target-wide, not per module.

regions.description: Sources grouped by where their code goes.

overlay.description: The overlay number, present only when `dest` is not `main`.

value.description: Null for a bare definition with no value.

origin.description: What put it there (a module, a component, or the project) so that a define appearing twice can be traced.
